meta.main_desc: Accurate, reliable information, subtypes, symptoms, and intelligent AI assistant support for Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID).

hero.subtitle: For children, young adults and families navigating ARFID: sensory mapping, safe Food Chaining, and empathetic AI companion guidance for anxiety-free meals.
hero.card_bubble: Based on your safe food crispy crackers, I formulated 2 gentle transition bridges that share the identical crunch profile while introducing essential micronutrients!

what_is.title: What is ARFID and Why is it Never 'Fussy Eating'?
what_is.subtitle: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder is a formal, neurobiologically influenced eating disorder, not a behavioral whim.
what_is.def_p1: is defined by significant food restriction regarding volume, variety, or sensory properties without concern for body shape or caloric intake.
what_is.def_p2: Unlike everyday picky eating, ARFID carries real clinical consequences: malnutrition, growth faltering, intense distress, and reliance on oral nutritional supplements or enteral feeding.
what_is.dsm5_tag: American Psychiatric Association (APA) DSM-5 Diagnostic Code
what_is.distinction_title: Zero Body Image or Weight Concerns
what_is.distinction_intro: Unlike Anorexia Nervosa or Bulimia, dietary restriction in ARFID is completely unrelated to physical appearance:
what_is.distinction_1: No fear of becoming overweight or gaining body fat.
what_is.distinction_2: Driven by sensory over-responsiveness, trauma, or low internal hunger cues.
what_is.distinction_3: It is an involuntary sensory/neurological reaction, never a lack of willpower.

who.title: Who Experiences ARFID and Why?
who.subtitle: ARFID spans across ages and demonstrates significant intersection with sensory processing differences and neurodivergence.
who.card1_desc: While frequently emerging in early development, it frequently persists into adolescence and adulthood if unaddressed.
who.card2_desc: Autistic and ADHD individuals experience significantly higher rates due to innate sensory processing sensitivity.
who.card3_desc: Past choking incidents, severe vomiting, GERD, or allergic anaphylaxis frequently catalyze persistent avoidance.
who.card4_desc: Genetic super-tasting and heightened oral-tactile sensitivity play key biological roles in defensive rejection.

symptoms.title: The 3 Primary ARFID Subtypes
symptoms.subtitle: In clinical practice, ARFID manifests through 3 distinct sensory and psychological pathways (or combinations thereof).
symptoms.type1_title: Lack of Interest in Food & Eating
symptoms.type1_desc: Difficulty recognizing interoceptive hunger cues, minimal intrinsic motivation to eat, and rapid fullness.
symptoms.type1_b1: Accidentally skipping meals or forgetting to eat
symptoms.type1_b2: Feeling uncomfortably full after minimal bites
symptoms.type1_b3: Perceiving eating as a tiring, burdensome chore
symptoms.type2_desc: Defensive responses to food textures, graininess, temperature inconsistencies, or strong aromas.
symptoms.type2_b1: Consuming only specific brands, consistent colors and packaging
symptoms.type2_b2: Extreme distress if distinct foods touch on the plate
symptoms.type2_b3: Gag reflex triggered by mixed, mushy, or stringy textures
symptoms.type3_desc: Profound panic regarding potential choking, gagging, vomiting, or allergic reaction during swallowing.
symptoms.type3_b1: Persistent fear that solid food will obstruct the airway
symptoms.type3_b2: Retreating exclusively to smooth liquids or baby purees
symptoms.type3_b3: Sympathetic nervous system arousal (fight-or-flight) at table
symptoms.gen_2: 🧪 Micronutrient Deficiencies (Iron, B12, Zinc, Vitamin D)
symptoms.gen_3: 🍱 Social Withdrawal (Avoiding cafeteria, parties, dining out)

treatment.title: How is ARFID Clinically Managed?
treatment.subtitle: ARFID cannot be solved through pressure, bribery, or starving out. Multidisciplinary protocols are mandatory.
treatment.card1_desc: Developed by Harvard specialists to gently dismantle mealtime terror through predictable, voluntary micro-exposures.
treatment.card2_desc: Gradually bridging from an accepted safe food to a novel food by subtly tweaking one sensory attribute at a time.
treatment.card3_desc: Desensitizing oral defensive reflexes and regulating tactile thresholds under licensed pediatric occupational therapists.
treatment.card4_desc: Continuous monitoring of cardiac rhythm, growth percentiles, and blood biochemistry by a physician.
treatment.card5_desc: Constructing calm, fortified meal plans that meet essential caloric requirements without triggering sensory alarm.
treatment.card6_desc: De-escalating dining room friction, relieving parental guilt, and establishing peaceful eating routines.

diagnosis.title: Vital Clinical Disclaimer
diagnosis.quote: "This digital platform and AI assistant DO NOT constitute a medical diagnosis, clinical treatment, or medical prescription. ARFID is a complex clinical eating disorder; all dietary adjustments and sensory interventions must be conducted in direct coordination with a licensed physician, child psychiatrist, and qualified clinical dietitian."
diagnosis.subtext: If experiencing severe malnutrition, sudden weight loss, or dysphagia, consult an accredited medical provider without delay.

assistant_sec.title: How Does Artificial Intelligence Assist in ARFID?
assistant_sec.subtitle: A gentle, zero-judgment companion analyzing food at the sensory physics level.
assistant_sec.card1_desc: The AI categorizes foods by acoustic crispness, viscosity, temperature, and visual homogeneity rather than plain calories.
assistant_sec.card2_desc: Constructs gentle transition trees from safe foods (e.g. golden fries) toward baked root vegetables with minimal perceptual shock.
assistant_sec.card3_desc: Detects hidden sensory triggers (onion slivers, tomato seeds) and recommends culinary techniques to ensure uniform safe consistency.
assistant_sec.card4_desc: Provides parents and individuals with calming, evidence-backed phrases and sensory regulation pauses during stressful moments.
assistant_sec.disclaimer_text: AI recommendations never supersede the care plan of your medical team; it serves strictly as a supportive home-environment aid.

cta.desc: Map your sensory preferences, catalog your safe foods, and explore thoughtful transitions with our understanding assistant.
